# Roadmap: function field arithmetic, part II

**Summary.** This roadmap extends FunctionFieldArithmetic from global arithmetic and ray class geometry to infinite roots of line bundles with sections and geometric class field theory with quadratic ramification. It builds coordinate comparisons over arbitrary commutative rings, the coherent infinite root stack and its fpqc quotient, the graded root Picard stack and its signed adelic presentation, symmetric lisse lines, high-degree Abel–Jacobi descent, and a normalized character sheaf in every integer degree. Its end theorem (§10.20) is that, for a geometrically connected double cover X′→X of smooth projective curves over a finite field of odd characteristic with reduced branch divisor R, the Frobenius trace function of the quadratic character sheaf on the root Picard stack equals the quadratic idele class character η_(F′/F) under the signed adelic presentation, with value +1 at split and −1 at inert unramified points (Yun–Zhang, Appendix A). Infinite roots and character sheaves share finite-root interfaces; the infinite tower is independent of the character-sheaf proof.

## Scope and ownership

FunctionFieldArithmetic §§2–4 owns completions, adeles, ideles, local and global Artin maps, ray characters and ordinary rigidified Picard geometry. This Part II begins with root data and retains their inertia, nilpotent sections and coherence. It owns the affine root torsor comparison, coherent infinite roots, fpqc Kummer towers and their DVR gerbes; root Picard objects, effective root divisors and signed adelic groupoids; symmetric local systems and their exterior cohomology; all-degree character descent; and ramified norms and trace comparison.

SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18–1.23 owns generic stackification, two-fibre products, quotient stacks, algebraicity, finite root stacks, their affine charts and full nonreduced finite branch fibres. Its §§3.3–3.7 own ordinary curve cohomology, Picard groupoids and stacks, degree components, universal sections, Abel maps and line-bundle norms. AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A–L0C owns tensor sections, tensor coherence, duals, polynomial powers and strong monoidal pullback. These constructions are imported. The finite DVR root chart, finite two-pullback presentation and finite affine quotient presentation are supplier contracts, rather than local targets. Coordinates, coframe signs, relative stack-base geometry and infinite coherent limits are the additional comparisons developed here.

Mathlib supplies polynomial quotients, their root relation and their finite presentation (`AdjoinRoot.finitePresentation`, used for the normalization algebra in every exponent), character-basis powers, tensor products, group algebras and directed colimits. Tau Ceti supplies the tensor/exterior projection, factorial and antisymmetrizer composites, their naturality, tensor permutation representation and finite-group corestriction. These are already in the library; only compatibility with the Koszul action and its invariant-image consequence remains a target. Ordinary finite-cover monodromy, scheme inertia, adic coefficients, scheme duality and Künneth are stated by EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.0.2, F.0.A1–F.0.A2, F.3a, F.4–F.6. DeligneWeightsAndPurity §8.24 owns rational étale coefficients on finite-type DM stacks, and GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands §1.4 owns the constructible derived categories of finite-type algebraic stacks with their six operations, perverse t-structure and intermediate extensions; both are imported. The finite-rank lisse descent and monodromy comparisons with their rank-one specialization, proper degree-zero base change, coarse-stalk calculations, and the perverse t-exactness of proper quasi-finite pushforward between tame DM stacks with its intermediate-extension comparison (§7.7) are targets in Layer 7, and the projective-space simple-connectivity input is in Layer 8. Unramified geometric class field theory in the Serre–Lang form, where abelian covers of a curve are pulled back from isogenies of its Jacobian, is PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology §RD.6.62; Layers 7–10 construct the ramified quadratic character sheaf instead. Symplectic central-L-value theory is outside this roadmap.

## Conventions

For Layers 1–3, A is an arbitrary commutative unital ring, including the zero ring, f∈A is arbitrary, and geometric root exponents satisfy n≥1. Auxiliary tensor powers allow n=0, with M⁰=O and t⁰=1. Write B_n=A[t]/(tⁿ−f). An object over T→X is (M,t,φ:Mⁿ≅L_T), with φ(tⁿ)=s_T. Every arrow is a line-bundle isomorphism preserving both the section and the identification. The ambient category of invertible sheaves also contains noninvertible maps; take its core. Tensor powers use fixed recursive parentheses with explicit canonical comparisons.

Finite roots use fppf descent without requiring n invertible. Étale Kummer requires n invertible. Infinite roots and torsors use fpqc descent. An index arrow m→n means n divides m and takes a root to its (m/n)-th power. Compatible systems retain comparison arrows and their cocycle. Factorial indices are d_i=(i+1)!, beginning at 1!, and the factorial-level root u_i satisfies the equation u_i^(d_i)=f; at i=0 the stage is A[t]/(t−f) with u_0=f, and at i=2 the relation is u_2^6=f, not u_2^3=f. The band is the affine group scheme D(ℚ/ℤ)=lim μ_n, including its infinitesimal points. All sites use fixed universes; enlargement claims range over the essential image with coherent lifts, never all objects of a larger universe.

A normalized coframe β:M≅O satisfies βⁿ=φ, with left action ζβ and coordinate β(t) of weight +1. This coframe action inverts the scalar band on the zero-section gerbe. The band-preserving Kummer coordinate uses Isom(x_λ,y) after a chosen origin; replacing λ by vλ multiplies that coordinate by [v]. Finite Kummer transitions take [a]_m to [a]_n with no extra power. As a sign witness, at n=2, β′=−β gives β′(t)=−β(t), while on the zero section the nontrivial automorphism is still labelled −1.

For Layers 4–10, k is finite of odd characteristic p, X/k is smooth projective geometrically connected, R⊂X is reduced finite, U=X−R, g is the genus, and ρ=deg_k R. Layer 4's frame comparisons also apply over any field of characteristic different from two with R finite étale. Divisor degree is weighted by residue degrees; after geometric splitting ρ counts geometric branch points. No rational point of degree one is chosen. Picard components are torsors, with their gerbes retained.

Write P^d for the degree-d root Picard stack: (L,K_R,ι:K_R²≅L|_R). Its section variant adds only α_R on R. The whole root-divisor stack adds a global section a with ι(α_R²)=a|_R. Its effective open requires a nonzero on every geometric curve fibre. For A=k[ε]/ε², a=ε on O has nonzero raw value but zero geometric-fibre value, so it is outside that open; the whole stack retains it. Full and relative inertia are different. For empty R the ordinary Picard scalar automorphisms remain.

Coefficients are ℚ̄_ℓ with ℓ≠p, interpreted through finite coefficient fields and their lattices with compatible scalar extension. Use geometric Frobenius. The symmetric lisse line L_d is unshifted, and L_d[d] is perverse. Permuting degree-zero sheaf lines has ordinary symmetry; swapping two degree-one cohomology classes contributes −1. Thus for independent e₁,e₂ the degree-two alternating tensor is e₁⊗e₂−e₂⊗e₁. Rational averaging inverts every factorial, including when ℓ divides it. Branch inertia has order dividing two; global rank-one monodromy can have order three or infinite image.

The uniform bound is B=ρ+max(2g−1,1). For d≥B put n=d−g+1 and a=n−ρ≥1. A split Abel–Jacobi fibre retains (u,α), and its section coordinate is (u,α²). The proper scalar quotient has weights (2^a,1^ρ) for ρ>0, and ordinary weight one for ρ=0. For g=0, ρ=1, d=2 the bound is 2, n=3, a=2 and weights are (2,2,1); setting α=0 leaves the two kernel coordinates, rather than identifying all points with their squared section coordinates.

For an idele a put E(a)=Σ_x v_x(a_x)x and associate O_X(−E(a)). Hence π_x⁻¹ has E=−x and gives O_X(x), of degree [k(x):k]. The signed right-action groupoid retains a generic frame and all modified-unit labels; quotienting further by F× gives the root Picard groupoid. The modified-unit map is not required injective. Norm statements use based torsor fibres, compatible nullhomotopies and H² obstructions. For the quadratic chart t²=a, the norm of c+dt is c²−ad², reducing to c² on a=0; this fixes the norm sign.

## Exact supplier contracts

### From Mathlib

Use `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme` and its module-sheaf and site APIs; `CategoryTheory.Core`; `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fppfTopology` and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fpqcTopology`; `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack` and `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.Grothendieck`. Stack descent on a pseudofunctor supplies no algebraic atlas by itself. Affine carriers are `AdjoinRoot`, `AdjoinRoot.eval₂_root`, `AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom`, `AdjoinRoot.algHom_ext` and `AdjoinRoot.powerBasis'` in `Mathlib/RingTheory/AdjoinRoot.lean`. Finite presentation of the normalization algebra D=B[T]/(Tⁿ−u) over B is the instance `AdjoinRoot.finitePresentation` of the same file, applied with coefficient algebra B over itself; it holds for every natural n, including n=0 where D=B[T]/(1−u) (which is B[T] when u=1), and for the zero ring, with no positivity or invertibility of n. Character calculations use `rootsOfUnity` in `Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/Basic.lean`, `MonoidAlgebra.single_pow` in `Mathlib/Algebra/MonoidAlgebra/Defs.lean`, and the group-algebra Hopf structure. Tensor products, `Module.Basis`, matrix determinant, kernels and module quotients supply the affine algebra. Use `DirectLimit.exists_eq_mk` in `Mathlib/Order/DirectedInverseSystem.lean:130` for a component representative of every directed-limit element; it requires the directed system, not any root-parameter hypothesis. Its applications to the factorial and positive-divisibility diagrams are imported in §§3.31–3.32. For a closed point of a finite-type ℚ-chart use `finite_of_finite_type_of_isJacobsonRing` in `Mathlib/RingTheory/Jacobson/Ring.lean:676`, applied to the finite-type residue quotient field.

The quotient-root relation gives t²=0 in 𝔽₂[t]/t² and t⁴=4 in ℤ[t]/(t²−2). At exponent zero it says 1=f in the quotient by 1−f; that quotient has no positive-exponent covering assertion. The total definitions `rootChart`, `rootChartCoaction` and `rootChartComparison` admit n=0 as quotient-algebra formulas: their unit-root factor is then A[h], and no μ₀ or Hopf-algebra interpretation is asserted. The action and sharp comparison theorems require n>0. A character e₁ satisfies e₁²=1 over 𝔽₂ even though μ₂ is non-étale. These Checks distinguish the quotient relation from reduced geometric points.

The lower-coordinate count is imported from `Finset.card_product_filter_lt` in `Mathlib/Data/Finset/Prod.lean` and `Nat.choose_two_right` in `Mathlib/Data/Nat/Choose/Basic.lean`: at n=0 and n=1 it is 0, at n=2 it is 1, and at n=3 it is 3.

## How to read the build

Layers 1–2 give finite-root coordinates and relative geometry; Layer 3 passes to coherent fpqc towers. Layers 4–6 independently build root Picard, effective-divisor and adelic interfaces. Layer 7 constructs symmetric lisse lines and their cohomology, Layer 8 proves effective descent, Layer 9 extends and normalizes in every degree, and Layer 10 identifies the quadratic trace. Each subsection states its exact hypotheses and proof inputs. A proof route is one way to establish the target; its named inputs identify the theory it uses. Every *Needs:* item precedes its consumer: the finite chart-point groupoid of §§1.20–1.22 is in Layer 1, finite-root fpqc descent (§2.4) precedes affine stackification (§2.7), and the stack coefficient interfaces of §§7.4–7.7 precede the symmetric lisse lines that use them.

## Layer 1: root coordinates and affine comparison

### 1.1 Diagonalizable action on the affine root chart

For a commutative ring A, f∈A and n≥1, each ζ∈rootsOfUnity(n,A) induces an A-algebra automorphism of the AdjoinRoot(Tⁿ−f) sending T to ζT. The construction is natural on A-algebras and represents the μ_n group-scheme action, including infinitesimal points.

The exponent n is a positive integer; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.

The construction has the following API.

- The distinguished quotient root maps to ζ times itself.
- Every coefficient from A is fixed.
- The automorphisms for ζξ and ζ composed with ξ agree.

A proof route uses the following steps. The image ζT satisfies Tⁿ−f because ζⁿ=1; use the quotient lift.
Use ζ⁻¹ for the inverse; generator evaluation proves identity and multiplication.
Apply the same construction on every A-algebra to retain the group-scheme action.

**Checks.**

- The unit root of unity acts as the identity.
- For n=2 the element −1 sends T to −T.
- On 𝔽_p[ε]/ε² at n=p, 1+ε has p-th power one and acts by T↦(1+ε)T.

In characteristic p the μ_p action is not detected by its geometric-point set.

([TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) line 778 — §3.1 pp.14–16, P=N and Corollary 3.13)

*Needs:* `AdjoinRoot`; `AdjoinRoot.eval₂_root`; `AdjoinRoot.lift`; `rootsOfUnity`.

### 1.2 Cyclic root coefficient permutation

For positive n, construct the equivalence σ:Fin n×Fin n≃Fin n×Fin n defined by σ(i,j)=(i,i+j) using cyclic addition on Fin n, with inverse σ⁻¹(i,k)=(i,k−i). Its representative is (i,(i+j) mod n); it reorders coordinates of the root action comparison.

n≥1. The construction is independent of the coefficient ring.

The construction has the following API.

- σ(i,j)=(i,i+j) in the cyclic Fin n group.
- σ⁻¹(i,k)=(i,k−i) in the cyclic Fin n group.
- The natural representative of the second component of σ(i,j) is (i+j) mod n.
- The second component of σ(i,j) is smaller than its first iff n≤i+j, for natural representatives 0≤i,j<n.

A proof route uses the following steps. Use the pinned cyclic additive group on Fin n, not addition of natural representatives without reduction.
Define the two pair maps and verify their composites by additive cancellation. No coefficient ring or choice of a root of unity enters.

**Checks.**

- At n=1 the permutation fixes every pair.
- At n=2, σ(1,1)=(1,0).
- At n=3, σ⁻¹(2,0)=(2,1); natural truncated subtraction would give the wrong answer.

At n=2 the wrapping position (1,1) maps to the lower position (1,0).

([TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) line 778 — §3.1 pp.14–16, character grading and Corollary 3.13, P=N; [STACKS-KUMMER](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/040N) line 1442 — Tag 040N, Lemma 59.28.3, unit-parameter finite-free cover and proof)

*Needs:* `Fin.addCommGroup`; `Fin.coe_int_add_eq_ite`.

### 1.3 Root comparison wrapping exponent

For n≥1 and p=(i,j) in Fin n×Fin n, floor((i+j)/n)=1 when n≤i+j and 0 otherwise, with i,j their natural representatives.

n≥1. Matrix and weight-product assertions use any commutative coefficient ring A and f∈A; index and sign assertions are independent of A. No nonzerodivisor, unit, reducedness or invertibility-of-n assumption.

A proof route uses the following steps. Each representative is smaller than n, hence its remainder is itself and its individual quotient is 0.
Split on the wrapping inequality. Import the two natural addition/division formulas to give quotient 1 or 0, retaining positivity of n.

**Checks.**

- At n=2 the column (1,1) has exponent 1.
- At n=2 the column (0,1) has exponent 0, so it contributes weight 1 rather than f.

This root-specific index assertion explains every column weight in the matrix; it does not add an invertibility assumption to A.

([STACKS-KUMMER](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/040N) line 1442 — Tag 040N, complete Lemma 59.28.3 statement and proof)

*Needs:* `Nat.add_div_eq_of_add_mod_lt`; `Nat.add_div_eq_of_le_mod_add_mod`.

### 1.4 Framed root coordinates

For arbitrary f in A and a commutative A-algebra B, store a bundled unit u and a root-section coordinate y with u*y^n=algebraMap(f). The unit records the power identification after choosing a frame; it is not assumed to have an n-th root. This coordinate carrier does not assert that a root line admits a global frame.

Use arbitrary commutative A and commutative A-algebra B in a common universe; f arbitrary. The coordinate carrier and its groupoid exist for every natural n; the chart embedding and normalization comparison use positive n via NeZero. No invertibility of n, reducedness, nontriviality, unit-section, regularity, finite-generation, flatness or injectivity assumption. A chosen-frame coordinate groupoid only. The sheaf RootObject-to-coordinate functor, existence of frames and unit roots locally, fppf stackification, effective descent, infinite coherent reindexing and genuine 2-limits are distinct targets.

The construction has the following API.

- Every framed root p satisfies p.u*p.y^n=algebraMap(f), with p.u a bundled unit.
- If a bundled unit w has w^n=p.u, then (w*p.y)^n=algebraMap(f). This gives a normalized chart root with no field, regularity or exponent-invertibility assumption.
- For every framed arrow h:p→q, q.y=h.label*p.y. No cancellation or regularity of the section is assumed.
- For every framed arrow h:p→q, q.u*h.label^n=p.u as an equality of bundled units. This retains the power-identification constraint even if the sections vanish.

A proof route uses the following steps. Use the unit type and retain the power-identification equation as a field.

Its underlying module comparison is the restriction of the imported equivalence QCoh(T)≃Desc_U(QCoh), not a descent functor on chosen frames. The equivalence descends the root line, its section, its power identification and every root arrow, with the tensor and pullback comparisons. It is compatible, up to specified natural isomorphisms, with refinement of covers and arbitrary base change of T.

Schemes and covers lie in one fixed universe-bounded site; category values may lie in a larger universe. No Noetherian, separation, finiteness or flatness hypothesis on a subsequent base-change map.

The construction has the following API.

- The functor D_U is an equivalence; its unit and counit are root isomorphisms with the underlying module descent unit and counit.
- The counit identifies the restriction of the descended t:O_T→M with t_i, through the unit and line-pullback comparisons.
- After the tensor-power pullback comparison, the counit carries the restricted descended φ and its inverse to φ_i and φ_i inverse.
- Compatible local isomorphisms descend uniquely to an isomorphism carrying t to t′ and satisfying φ′∘a^n=φ; neither condition is omitted.
- For a refinement V→U, the two effective-descent equivalences are compared by their unique root isomorphism inducing the refinement counit; identity and composite refinements satisfy the triangle and pentagon.
- Pulling the descent datum to Y→T and then descending is naturally isomorphic to pulling the descended root to Y; the comparison preserves t,φ and has the pullback identity/composition laws.

A proof route uses the following steps. Use SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.22 (quasi-coherent descent) on all quasi-coherent modules and all linear maps. Descend M_i and the transition isomorphisms; finite-locally-free-descent, including rank, makes the result a invertible sheaf.
Through the imported strong symmetric monoidal pullback, identify the descended tensor power with M^n and the descended unit with O_T. Descend t_i as maps O→M and descend φ_i:M_i^n→L_i and φ_i inverse. Faithfulness checks that these maps are inverse and that φ(t^n)=s.
Fullness descends each compatible root arrow and its inverse; faithfulness detects its two defining squares, equality and the cocycle. This proves full faithfulness as well as essential surjectivity.
Compare two effective descents by the unique isomorphism inducing their local comparison. The same uniqueness proves refinement, base-change, identity and composition coherence; no chosen global frame enters.

**Checks.**

- For the singleton identity cover, D_U is equivalent to the identity root functor with its pullback-unit isomorphism.
- For n=2 over ℚ and the zero root section, the arrows with unit labels 1 and −1 remain distinct after descent along any fpqc cover; replacing the fibres by isomorphism classes fails this test.
- For the Zariski cover of P¹_Q by its two standard affines, descend local frames of M=O(1), t=0, φ:M^2≅L=O(2). The descended root line is O(1), which has no global frame.
- For the root (O,t=2,φ=identity) of (O,4) over ℤ and n=2, base change to 𝔽₂ descends to the zero-section root. The comparison does not cancel t or require Z→𝔽₂ flat.

Every descent object is recovered with its section and power identification. D_U induces a bijection on every Hom set, including the automorphisms of a zero-section root.

### 3.12 Limits of finite flat torsor towers

Unlike AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry §4.23’s field-gerbe limit, this target treats arbitrary scheme bases T and explicit torsor towers. Let T be a scheme. Let G_n (n ≥ 1) be commutative group schemes over T, each finite locally free, with homomorphisms π(n,m): G_m → G_n for n|m such that π(n,n) is the identity, π(n,m)π(m,l) = π(n,l), and each π(n,m) is faithfully flat with finite locally free kernel. Put G = lim G_n, an affine flat group scheme over T. Let P_n be fppf G_n-torsors with π(n,m)-equivariant T-morphisms p(n,m): P_m → P_n, p(n,n) = id and p(n,m)p(m,l) = p(n,l). Then: (a) each p(n,m) is a torsor under ker π(n,m), hence finite locally free and surjective; (b) the limit P = lim P_n exists, is affine over T, and over an affine open U ⊆ T its coordinate ring is the directed colimit of those of the P_n|U; (c) P → T is faithfully flat, so {P → T} is an fpqc covering; (d) the action map G ×_T P → P ×_T P, (g,x) ↦ (gx,x), is an isomorphism, so P is an fpqc G-torsor, and for every n the G-map P → P_n induces an isomorphism P ×^G G_n ≅ P_n of G_n-torsors; (e) formation of P commutes with every base change T′ → T; (f) G-equivariant T-morphisms P → Q between two such limits correspond bijectively to compatible families of G_n-equivariant morphisms P_n → Q_n; (g) for every fpqc G-torsor Q the pushforwards Q_n = Q ×^G G_n are fppf G_n-torsors and the canonical map Q → lim Q_n is an isomorphism. Hence fpqc G-torsors and such towers, with equivariant maps, form equivalent groupoids. Neither finite presentation of P nor fppf-local triviality of P is asserted.

T is an arbitrary scheme; the index set is the positive integers ordered by divisibility, which is directed. Each G_n is finite locally free over T and each transition G_m → G_n is faithfully flat with finite locally free kernel. For G_n = μ_n,T and ζ ↦ ζ^(m/n) the transition is the qth-power map, q = m/n: the coordinate ring of μ_m is free of rank q over that of μ_n, and the kernel is μ_q. Each P_n is an fppf G_n-torsor; the tower maps are equivariant and compose exactly.

A proof route uses the following steps. (a) Fppf locally on T choose a section of P_m, so P_m ≅ G_m; then p(n,m) becomes π(n,m) followed by a translation of G_n. π(n,m) is finite, flat and of finite presentation with kernel K = ker π(n,m), and G_m ×_(G_n) G_m ≅ G_m × K, so it is a K-torsor. These properties are fpqc local on the base (Stacks 02KY, 02L2, 02LA).
(b) The transition maps are finite, hence affine, and P_1 is finite over T, so the limit exists and is computed affine-locally (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.9 `affine_transition_limits`; Stacks-finite-root-projections-codex-7e92bd line 46, Lemma 32.2.1, tag 01YW, and line 51, Lemma 32.2.2, tag 01YX). Over U = Spec R it is Spec of the directed colimit of the coordinate rings of the P_n|U.
(c) Each P_n|U is finite locally free and surjective over U, so its coordinate ring is a faithfully flat R-algebra; a directed colimit of faithfully flat R-algebras is faithfully flat (Stacks 090N). Translate with flat_and_surjective_iff_faithfullyFlat_of_isAffine. P is affine over T, hence quasi-compact, and {P → T} is an fpqc covering.
(d) Fibre products commute with limits: G ×_T P = lim(G_n ×_T P_n) and P ×_T P = lim(P_n ×_T P_n), and the action map is the limit of the finite action isomorphisms. The G-map P → P_n factors through P ×^G G_n (pushforward along G → G_n, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.3 NonabelianH1.map and §1.16), a G_n-map of G_n-torsors, hence an isomorphism (§1.15 Torsor.hom_isIso).
(e) Pullback of affine schemes is tensor product of coordinate rings, and tensor product commutes with directed colimits. (f) is the universal property of the limit together with equivariance at each finite stage.
(g) Q_n is an fpqc G_n-torsor. It is representable by a T-scheme affine over T, by effective fpqc descent of affine morphisms (Stacks 0245; SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.1), and it is finite locally free and surjective over T because these properties descend. So Q_n → T is an fppf covering that trivializes Q_n. The map Q → lim Q_n is a G-map of G-torsors by (d), hence an isomorphism; Talpo–Vistoli sketch this direction in Remark 3.9.

Roots of 2: for G_n = μ_n over Spec ℚ and P_n = Spec ℚ[z_n]/(z_n^n − 2) with z_n = z_m^(m/n), P = Spec colim ℚ[z_n]/(z_n^n − 2) is an fpqc G-torsor with no ℚ-point (§3.65 (a Kummer limit torsor without fppf trivialization)). Trivial tower: P_n = G_n with p(n,m) = π(n,m) gives P = G with its translation action. Faithful flatness in (c) is proved on coordinate rings from the faithfully flat finite stages; nonemptiness of geometric fibres alone is not used. The comparison of (d) at each n is an isomorphism of G_n-torsors, not only of schemes.

([TV17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.1164v2) line 733 — Remark 3.9, p.15 For a projective system of affine group schemes of finite type with limit G, the remark sketches that a G-torsor is the projective limit of its pushforwards to the finite stages; this is direction (g). ### 3.190 The infinite DVR zero-section gerbe

For a DVR with residue field k, the zero-section gerbe of §3.179 in the closed fibre of the infinite root stack is the two-limit of the root gerbes of the normal line N, banded by G_k=lim_n μ_n, the fpqc inverse-limit group scheme over k, the diagonalizable group D(ℚ/ℤ)=Spec k[ℚ/ℤ] with character group ℚ/ℤ. In characteristic p each projection G_k→μ_(p^r) is a faithfully flat quotient map corresponding to the inclusion of characters ℤ/p^r⊂ℚ/ℤ; these projections are not subgroup inclusions, and Hom(μ_(p^r),G_k)=0 because a homomorphism of character groups ℚ/ℤ→ℤ/p^r is zero, ℚ/ℤ being divisible. G_k is nonetheless nonreduced in characteristic p: in k[ℚ/ℤ] the element e_[1/p]−1 is nonzero and (e_[1/p]−1)^p=e_[1]−1=0. It is the quotient of the explicitly reduced affine chart C_k(0)_red=k of §3.179, and it is noncanonically equivalent to B_kG_k: a chosen frame of N gives a compatible neutralization. The neutralization is not part of the canonical root stack.

Finite roots are defined fppf and satisfy the stronger fpqc descent theorem. Infinite systems and infinite torsors use fpqc descent.

A proof route uses the following steps. Setting the root section to zero identifies the zero-section substack of each finite closed fibre with the n-th root gerbe of N (§3.179).
A trivialization of that one-dimensional k-space supplies compatible trivial root objects at all n.
The automorphisms form lim μ_n, and coherent descent gives the banded gerbe. In residue characteristic zero this is the reduced fibre of B24; in every characteristic the zero-section gerbe and the reduced-chart quotient of §3.179 replace a reduction functor on infinite fpqc stacks.

The full fibre retains nilpotent finite charts; only the zero-section gerbe is identified with the classifying gerbe.

- In C_k(0)=colim k[z_n]/(z_n^n), z_n^r≠0 for r<n, whereas the reduced chart is k; the full fibre, the zero-section gerbe and its neutralization are three distinct objects.
- In characteristic p, every homomorphism μ_p→G_k is trivial: composed with the projection to μ_n it factors through μ_(np)→μ_n, and on characters the compatible map ℤ/n→ℤ/p is multiplication by p composed with a map, hence zero; so μ_p is a quotient of G_k, not a subgroup. In characteristic 2 the coordinate algebra k[ℚ/ℤ] has (e_[1/2]−1)²=e_[1]−1=0 with e_[1/2]−1≠0 by the group-algebra basis, so G_k is nonreduced, and the projection G_k→μ_2 remains faithfully flat. Replacing G_k by the étale group of its k̄-points, the prime-to-p part of Ẑ(1), loses this nonreduced structure; a wrong model with a subgroup μ_p would give a nonzero map μ_p→G_k.

### Examples

In the roots-of-two tower over ℚ, degrees n! of the minimal polynomials X^(n!)−2 are unbounded by Eisenstein at 2. Choose a closed point of a nonempty affine finite-type ℚ-chart in a proposed fppf cover. By Zariski’s lemma (`finite_of_finite_type_of_isJacobsonRing`, `Mathlib/RingTheory/Jacobson/Ring.lean:676`) its residue field is finite over ℚ, of some degree d, so it cannot contain a root of Xⁿ−2 for n>d, and hence cannot contain the compatible root family. The affine limit is an fpqc torsor and has no section on any nonempty fppf cover. For a unit family (ζ_n), the transition ζ_6³=ζ_2 corresponds to 1/2=3/6 in ℚ/ℤ. (STACKS-KUMMER line 1442, Lemma 59.28.3; the finite-stage degree argument is the one in §§3.53 and 3.65.)

**Checks.**

- In Spec ℚ[T], the closed point (T) has residue ℚ of degree 1; it cannot contain a root of X²−2, whose minimal degree is 2.
- The closed point (T²−2) has residue ℚ(√2) of degree 2; it contains √2 but cannot contain a root of X³−2, whose minimal degree is 3.
- The generic point (0) has residue ℚ(T), of infinite degree over ℚ since 1,T,T²,… are linearly independent. It is not a closed point and does not satisfy the finiteness step.

## Layer 4: The graded root Picard stack

### 4.1 The graded root Picard stack

Pic_X^√R(S) is the groupoid of (L,K_R,ι), where L is a line bundle on X×S, K_R a line bundle on R×S and ι:K_R²≅L|_(R×S). Its degree-d component imposes degree d on every geometric fibre; d ranges over all integers. Tensor product and dual give the graded commutative Picard stack.

Throughout this subsection, k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are ℚ̄_ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

The construction has the following API.

- Create (L,K_R,ι) from the two line bundles and the square identification.
- The degree is the fibrewise degree of L, additive under tensor product.
- Tensor two objects and their root identifications; dual gives inverse up to coherent isomorphism.
- Forget K_R,ι to the ordinary Picard stack.

A proof route uses the following steps. Import the ordinary line-bundle Picard stack and restriction to R.
Take the root-gerbe two-pullback for the restricted line bundle; do not require a section.
Tensor and dual root data with the imported coherent line-bundle isomorphisms.

**Checks.**

- At R=∅ this is the ordinary graded Picard stack.
- Negative-degree components contain line bundles and are not declared empty.
- Over an algebraically closed field with r geometric branch points, forgetting roots has relative stabilizer μ₂^r.

Pic^d is a torsor component, with no chosen degree-one point required.

Along S′→S pull back both lines and transport ι using the canonical tensor and pullback-composition comparisons. This defines the scheme-site stack refining the imported underlying root-picard; its projection to the ordinary Picard stack forgets K and ι. No section of either line is part of this definition.

k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms. Line bundles are TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.

- For k′/k, the root stack for (X_k′,R_k′) identifies with restriction to k′-schemes, compatibly with forget and pullback.

### Examples

For X=ℙ¹, R={0,∞}, d=1, the two incidence divisors are distinct points and their intersection is empty. For d=2 they meet in the single divisor 0+∞ with codimension 2. At 2·0 the target inertia is μ₂ and the ordered source inertia is μ₂²; multiplication has diagonal kernel μ₂. The full target fibre retains the square-zero root.

## Layer 6: Signed adelic root groupoids

### 6.1 Modified local units at ramified places

At x∈R let O_(√x)×={(u,v)∈O_x××k(x)× : ū=v²}, with componentwise multiplication. For x∉R use O_x×. Let O_(√R)× be their product. Its map to adelic units forgets v and has kernel ∏_(x∈R)μ₂(k(x)); do not assume it is injective.

Throughout this subsection, k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are ℚ̄_ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

The construction has the following API.

- Create (u,v) with ū=v².
- Project to u in O_x× and to the corresponding idele unit.
- The kernel consists of u=1 and v²=1.

A proof route uses the following steps. Use FunctionFieldArithmetic §§2.1 and 4.8’s local completions, valuation-ring units and residue map.
Take the fibre product of multiplicative groups along reduction and the square homomorphism.
Form the finite modification of the ordinary unit product, with its map to ideles.

**Checks.**

- At R=∅ the product is the ordinary unit product.
- At a ramified place, (1,−1) is a nontrivial kernel element.
- A unit with nonsquare residue has no lift to this group.

The square operation on residue elements is not additive in odd characteristic; no fibre-product ring is defined here.

### 6.2 Root lines with a generic trivialization

Let G_R(X) be the groupoid of (L,K_R,ι,τ_η), where (L,K_R,ι) is the k-point of Pic_X^√R and τ_η:L|Spec F≅F is an F-linear trivialization. An arrow (φ,ψ) satisfies φ|R∘ι=ι′∘ψ^(⊗2) and τ′_η∘φ_η=τ_η. Tensor product multiplies generic trivializations, the unit has its standard generic trivialization, and duality inverts it. Forgetting τ_η maps to the root Picard groupoid. Degree is deg L and may have either sign.

k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, F=k(X), and R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, possibly empty. Places are all closed points of X, including the points outside an affine chart. F_x is the normalized completed valuation field, O_x its valuation ring, and κ_x its residue field. The curve/place and residue identifications use the named suppliers. I=∏′_x F_x× relative to O_x×; U=∏_x O_x×; H=O_(√R)× is the modified-unit group. Write p:H→I for its homomorphism. Local root-unit coordinates satisfy ū_x=v_x².

The construction has the following API.

- Build an object from a root-line triple and an generic-fibre isomorphism.
- Forget the generic trivialization to Pic_X^√R(k), on both objects and arrows.
- Two arrows are equal exactly when their line-bundle and root-line isomorphisms agree; a root label is never inferred from the line isomorphism alone.
- A pair of isomorphisms is an arrow exactly when it respects both the root square diagram and the displayed generic-frame equality.
- Tensor the line bundles, roots, square identifications and generic frames; associators, unitors and symmetry are coherently.
- Dualize all data and invert the generic trivialization, with the usual evaluation isomorphisms to the unit.
- Return deg L; this is invariant under arrows, additive under tensor product and negated by duality.
- For f∈F× multiply τ_η by f. This is an F× action with identity and composition laws; forgetting the frame is invariant under it.

A proof route uses the following steps. Add only a generic trivialization to the root-line triple; use its line-bundle isomorphisms, tensor product and duality.
Restrict arrows to those preserving the generic frame. The square-root diagram remains part of each arrow, so root automorphisms are retained.
Tensor, dual, restriction and their coherence are imported from Layer 4 and the ordinary Picard-groupoid supplier.

**Checks.**

- For R=∅, forgetting root data identifies G_∅ with ordinary generically trivialized line bundles; through the ordinary divisor dictionary it is equivalent to the discrete groupoid of signed divisors.
- For f∈F× with nonzero principal divisor, the trivial root line at R=∅ with generic frames 1 and f gives nonisomorphic objects of G_∅, although forgetting the generic frame gives the same line bundle.
- On X=P¹ over F₅ with R={0}, take L=O_X, K_R=F₅ and τ_η=1. The square identifications with coefficients 1 and 2 give nonisomorphic objects of G_R, both of valuation divisor 0.
- For every A, A⊗A^∨ is isomorphic to the unit with its standard generic frame; its degree is 0, even when A has negative degree.

The forgetful functor remembers the entire root-line triple and forgets exactly the generic frame. No section or effectivity condition is added; G_R is defined in all realized degrees.

### 6.6 The signed root-divisor groupoid

Define Div^√R(X) to be the action groupoid A_F×/O_(√R)× for the homomorphism O_(√R)×→A_F×. It contains signed divisors in all degrees; neither quotient by F× nor an effectivity condition is imposed. With this valuation convention its Abel–Jacobi functor lands in the double quotient Pic_X^√R(k) and has underlying line bundle O_X(−E(a)), with the retained square-root line along R. The quadratic character is pulled back along this functor. Effective section moduli are a separate construction; they are not identified with this entire groupoid.

Throughout this subsection, k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are ℚ̄_ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

The construction has the following API.

- An idele a determines its object in the right-action groupoid.
- A modified unit h gives the arrow a→a·forget(h); its label h is retained even when forget(h)=1.
- The ordinary signed divisor is E(a)=Σ_x v_x(a_x)x, and modified-unit arrows preserve it.
- Idele multiplication supplies addition of root divisors; identity and inverse give the unit and additive inverse, with their groupoid coherence.
- The right quotient maps to F×\A_F×/O_(√R)×; its underlying line is O_X(−E) in the stated valuation convention.
- The automorphism group of every idele object is ker(O_(√R)×→A_F×)=∏_(x∈R)μ₂(k(x)); at R=∅ it is trivial.

Use FunctionFieldArithmetic §§2.1 and 4.8’s divisor/idele dictionary E(a)=Σv_x(a_x)x to obtain the ordinary signed divisor, without imposing nonnegative valuations or dividing by F×.
Apply the canonical functor to the double quotient and YZ19 Lemma A.5. Its sign is fixed by a uniformizer π_x⁻¹: E=−x and the associated Picard line is O_X(x). At branch points retain the root line and square isomorphism.
Pull back the idele character along this Abel–Jacobi functor.

- For x∉R the idele equal to π_x⁻¹ at x and 1 elsewhere has E=−x and Abel–Jacobi line O_X(x).
- At any branch point in odd characteristic, the modified unit with u=1,v=−1 there and identity elsewhere gives a nonidentity automorphism of the unit idele.

### 7.1 Koszul-signed permutation action on tensor powers

Let K be a commutative ring, V a K-module and d≥0. The Koszul-signed action of S_d=Perm({1,…,d}) on the tensor power V^(⊗d) sends σ to sgn(σ)·P_σ, where P_σ(v_1⊗⋯⊗v_d)=v_(σ⁻¹(1))⊗⋯⊗v_(σ⁻¹(d)) is Tau Ceti's permutation representation PiTensorProduct.reindexRepresentation. It is a representation of S_d by K-linear maps, natural in V. It is the S_d-action on the degree-d summand of the graded tensor power of a graded module concentrated in cohomological degree one: exchanging two factors of odd degree contributes −1. On a tensor power of degree-zero factors the same permutation acts by P_σ, without sign.

K is a commutative ring, V any K-module and d a natural number. In Layer 7 the case used is K=ℚ̄_ℓ and V=H¹(X⊗k̄,j_*L)≅H¹(X_1^√R⊗k̄,L), on which geometric Frobenius acts K-linearly.

The construction has the following API.

- For σ∈S_d, the K-linear endomorphism sgn(σ)·P_σ of V^(⊗d).
- σ·(v_1⊗⋯⊗v_d)=sgn(σ)·v_(σ⁻¹(1))⊗⋯⊗v_(σ⁻¹(d)).
- The identity permutation acts as the identity.
- στ acts as the composite of the actions of σ and τ.
- The representation S_d→End_K(V^(⊗d)), σ↦sgn(σ)P_σ.
- The action is sgn(σ) times Tau Ceti's unsigned PiTensorProduct.reindexRepresentation.
- For d=2 the transposition sends v⊗w to −w⊗v.
- For K-linear f:V→W, f^(⊗d)∘σ_V=σ_W∘f^(⊗d); for a Frobenius acting K-linearly on V this is Frobenius equivariance.

A proof route uses the following steps. P_σ is the reindexing of the tensor factors along σ, and σ↦P_σ is already a representation (tauceti:PiTensorProduct.reindexRepresentation).
sgn:S_d→{±1} is a homomorphism with values in the centre of End_K(V^(⊗d)), so σ↦sgn(σ)P_σ is again a representation.
For a K-linear f:V→W, use mathlib:PiTensorProduct.map_reindex to commute f^(⊗d) with P_σ, then with its sign twist. The Tau Ceti commute_reindexRepresentation_map citation covers the endomorphism case only.

**Checks.**

- For d=0 every element of V^(⊗0)≅K is invariant.
- For d=1 every element of V^(⊗1)≅V is invariant.
- If 2 is invertible in K, the invariants of the action on K^(⊗2) are zero.
- If 2 is invertible, x⊗x is invariant under the unsigned permutation action but is invariant under the Koszul-signed action only when x⊗x=0; a definition omitting the sign gives symmetric tensors.
- Over ℤ/2 the sign is trivial: the invariants of (ℤ/2)^(⊗2) are the whole line although ∧²(ℤ/2)=0.

For d=2 and V=K the transposition acts on K⊗K≅K by −1, while P_σ alone acts by +1. For d≤1 the group S_d is trivial and the action is the identity.

### 7.2 Rational averaging: invariants are exact and commute with linear functors

Let G be a finite group and K a commutative ring in which |G| is invertible. (i) For a K-linear representation V, e_V=|G|⁻¹Σ_(g∈G)g is an idempotent with image V^G, and V↦V^G is exact: an equivariant surjection is surjective on invariants. (ii) In a K-linear additive category in which idempotents split (for example any abelian category, such as constructible ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaves on a scheme), the invariants A^G of an object with a G-action are the image of e_A, and every K-linear additive functor F satisfies F(A^G)≅F(A)^G naturally, because F(e_A)=e_(F(A)). In particular H^i(Y,A^G)≅H^i(Y,A)^G for a sheaf A with a G-action on a scheme Y, and q_* of invariants is the invariants of q_*.

G finite; |G| a unit in K. Over ℚ̄_ℓ this holds for every finite G, including groups of order divisible by ℓ.

A proof route uses the following steps. e is fixed by left and right multiplication by G and e²=e (mathlib:GroupAlgebra.average); its image is V^G (mathlib:Representation.isProj_averageMap; tauceti:Representation.range_norm_eq_invariants).
Exactness: if f:V→W is equivariant and onto and w∈W^G, choose v with f(v)=w; then e_V(v) is invariant and f(e_V v)=e_W(w)=w.
A preadditive category in which idempotents have kernels, for example an abelian category, is idempotent complete (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Idempotents.isIdempotentComplete_iff_idempotents_have_kernels); any additive functor preserves split idempotents and their images (Stacks §12.4), and K-linearity gives F(e_A)=e_(F(A)).

### 7.4 Finite-rank lisse descent and finite-cover monodromy

Let 𝒳 be a normal finite-type Deligne–Mumford stack over a finite field k, let ℓ≠char k, and fix a finite extension E/ℚ_ℓ with ring of integers O_E and uniformizer ϖ. Construct the integral lattice category by étale-atlas descent of lisse O_E-sheaves that are locally free of finite rank, the rank being locally constant on 𝒳 and allowed to be zero, with all O_E-linear sheaf morphisms between them; it is equivalent to compatible systems of locally free finite-rank O_E/ϖᵐ-local systems with their reduction isomorphisms for m≥1. Finite coefficient reduction is a functor on this integral category. Inverting ϖ on morphisms, that is replacing each Hom module M by M⊗_(O_E)E, gives the equivalence with the lisse E-sheaves admitting a global lisse O_E-lattice in DeligneWeightsAndPurity §8.24’s rational category; on the rational side the lattice is a presentation, not part of the object. On a connected nonempty 𝒳 with a geometric base point x̄, the fibre at x̄ identifies the integral category with continuous representations of π₁(𝒳,x̄), the fundamental group of representable finite étale covers, on finite free O_E-modules, and the rational category with continuous representations on finite-dimensional E-vector spaces; every such rational representation preserves an O_E-lattice because π₁(𝒳,x̄) is compact. Pullback, tensor product, internal Hom, dual and Frobenius descent commute with the equivalences at their integral and rational levels; reduction commutes with them at the integral level. No finite-reduction functor is asserted on the rational localization. Passing to finite coefficient fields and extending scalars defines the stated ℚ̄_ℓ category. Maps and objects descend along an étale atlas with the overlap cocycle retained. The rank-one objects are exactly the tensor-invertible ones, closed under tensor product and dual, with the dual as tensor inverse; this rank-one specialization, with its tensor and unit comparisons, is the input of the character-sheaf targets. For the smooth Artin stacks used in Layer 8, use smooth atlases to define the category of locally free finite-rank lisse sheaves by the same descent data, as a full subcategory of the lisse-étale category of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands §1.4, without asserting a profinite-representation dictionary for arbitrary Artin stacks.

The construction has the following API.

- For every étale atlas, objects and morphisms of the integral and rational categories are descent data of finite-rank lisse sheaves on the atlas, with the overlap cocycle retained; the descended categories are independent of the atlas through the refinement comparisons of DeligneWeightsAndPurity §8.24.
- For every m≥1, reduction modulo ϖᵐ is a functor on the integral category commuting with pullback, tensor product, dual and Frobenius descent.
- Localization is the identity on objects and M↦M⊗_(O_E)E on Hom modules, and is essentially surjective onto the lisse rational objects admitting a global lattice.
- On a connected nonempty 𝒳 with geometric base point x̄, the fibre functor at x̄ is an equivalence from the integral category to continuous π₁(𝒳,x̄)-representations on finite free O_E-modules, and from the rational category to continuous finite-dimensional E-representations; rank zero corresponds to the zero representation.
- For a morphism g:𝒴→𝒳 of connected nonempty normal DM stacks and a path from g(ȳ) to x̄, pullback along g corresponds to restriction of representations along π₁(𝒴,ȳ)→π₁(𝒳,x̄). In particular, when this map is surjective, as for a nonempty dense open substack of a connected normal 𝒳 (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.5.7), pullback is fully faithful in every finite rank.
- Tensor product, internal Hom and dual correspond to those of representations; on rank-one objects the dual is a tensor inverse and the unit comparison has scalar 1.

A proof route transports the finite-level scheme dictionary between finite locally constant sheaves and finite continuous π₁-modules (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.2) across the atlas, level by level in m, using Noohi's Galois category of representable finite étale covers, and passes to the inverse limit over m. The integral equivalence is localized only after its reduction functors are defined; normality and the stated lattice domain are retained.

**Checks.**

- On Bμ₂ over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic, the trivial line has invariant space of dimension 1 and the sign line has invariant space of dimension 0. Coarse-space lines alone would miss the latter.
- On Spec 𝔽₅, multiplication by 3 on the constant ℤ₃-lattice is not invertible and reduces to 0 on 𝔽₃, whereas multiplication by 2 is invertible and reduces to multiplication by 2. After localization, multiplication by 3 is invertible on ℚ₃; reducing that rational isomorphism would contradict preservation of isomorphisms.
- On the identity atlas, the tensor unit comparison has scalar 1; rescaling it by 2 fails the unit law.
- For k=𝔽₅, E=ℚ₃ and the arithmetic character sending Frobenius to 4, its reductions have eigenvalues 1 modulo 3 and 4 modulo 9, of orders 1 and 3. The ℚ₃-character has infinite image; requiring finite global image would wrongly exclude it.
- On ℙ¹ over 𝔽₅, pull back from Spec 𝔽₅ the lattice ℤ₃² on which Frobenius acts by J=[[1,1],[0,1]], so that Jⁿ=[[1,n],[0,1]]. Modulo 3 the action has order 3 and modulo 9 order 9, while the ℚ₃-action has infinite image. The only invariant line is spanned by the first basis vector, so the object is not a sum of rank-one objects, and its endomorphisms are the matrices [[a,b],[0,a]], of dimension 2. ### 7.5 Proper base change for the maps used in descent

Let f:𝒴→𝒳 be a proper morphism of finite-type algebraic stacks over k such that after every smooth scheme atlas T→𝒳 the source 𝒴_T is a separated tame Deligne–Mumford stack of finite presentation over T. Smooth-atlas descent supplies f_* and this comparison; its stalk at a geometric point x is H⁰(𝒴_x,F). The comparisons satisfy identity and composition equations and commute with coefficient reduction whenever those reductions commute with the displayed fibre invariants. For rational coefficients and finite relative stabilizers the higher group cohomology vanishes by averaging. In particular these statements apply to the ordered root-divisor map and to the proper weighted scalar quotient over a scheme in Layer 8. This theorem alone does not assert that f_* of a lisse sheaf is lisse; Layer 8 proves that using its fibre geometry.

The API consists of the degree-zero proper base-change isomorphism, its geometric-stalk formula, functoriality in F and in base change, and the compatible adic comparison when the stated reduction condition holds.

- For Bμ₂ with integral 2-adic sign coefficients, invariants are 0 but modulo 2 the sign becomes trivial and invariants are 𝔽₂. Thus coefficient reduction does not commute automatically; the extra reduction condition is necessary.

### 7.6 Rational coarse pushforward and nilpotent invariance

For a separated tame Deligne–Mumford stack 𝒴 of finite type over k with coarse space c:𝒴→Y, and a constructible rational ℓ-adic sheaf F, the geometric stalk of Rⁱc_*F at y is Hⁱ(G_y,F_ỹ), where ỹ is a lift with finite stabilizer G_y. Consequently Rⁱc_*F=0 for i>0, (c_*F)_y=(F_ỹ)^(G_y), and the Leray map Hʲ(Y,c_*F)→Hʲ(𝒴,F) is an isomorphism for every j. All identifications commute with rational coefficient extension and base change. Étale coefficient categories and their cohomology are invariant under nilpotent closed thickenings of DM stacks, by the corresponding scheme equivalence on an étale atlas; thus a full nonreduced geometric fibre may be replaced by its reduced residual gerbe for this calculation. No equality of these fibres as stacks is asserted.

The API consists of the coarse stalk and higher-image formulas, the Leray comparison, and the nilpotent-thickening pullback equivalence, compatible with the atlas and proper base-change maps.

- For the trivial C₂-module 𝔽₂, H¹(C₂,𝔽₂)=𝔽₂ has dimension 1; the rational vanishing formula cannot be imposed on those coefficients.

### 7.8 Local systems on the root curve and inertia of order two

Let 𝒳=X_1^√R and let ū be a geometric point of U⊂𝒳. Restriction to U is fully faithful from ℚ̄_ℓ-local systems on 𝒳 to ℚ̄_ℓ-local systems on U. Its essential image consists of the local systems whose monodromy, restricted to the inertia subgroup I_x̄⊂π1(U,ū) of every geometric point x̄ of X above R (for one, equivalently every, path), has order dividing two. In rank one: rank-one local systems on 𝒳 correspond to continuous characters χ:π1(U,ū)→ℚ̄_ℓ^× of the arithmetic fundamental group over k with χ(τ)²=1 for all τ in every I_x̄. Such χ is tamely ramified at R, since the wild inertia is pro-p with p odd. The global monodromy is unrestricted: an unramified χ of order three, or of infinite order, is allowed. At a geometric point of 𝒳 over x∈R the stabilizer μ₂ acts on the stalk through χ|I_x̄, which is trivial or the character of order two; χ|I_x̄ is trivial for every x exactly when the local system descends to X.

Throughout this subsection, k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are ℚ̄_ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used. Local systems are lisse ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaves of finite rank. π1(𝒳) is the fundamental group of the Galois category of representable finite étale covers of the Deligne–Mumford curve 𝒳 (Noohi §4), and local systems on 𝒳 of every finite rank, including zero, are continuous representations of it (§7.4 (finite-rank lisse descent and finite-cover monodromy)). The stacks and atlas charts used here are normal. Coefficient objects are defined over a finite extension E/ℚ_ℓ before scalar extension to ℚ̄_ℓ; no representation dictionary is asserted for arbitrary nonnormal stacks.

A proof route uses the following steps. U is a dense open substack of the connected normal Deligne–Mumford curve 𝒳 (§2.14 (regularity) and §2.15 (the exact DM locus)), so π1(U,ū)→π1(𝒳,ū) is surjective by InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.5.7. Restriction of continuous representations along this surjection is fully faithful in every finite rank; the finite-rank dictionary of §7.4 and its pullback compatibility transport it to lisse sheaves.
Étale-locally at x∈R with local equation s, 𝒳 is [Spec A[t]/(t²−s)/μ₂] (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21, SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.18–1.23). A local system on U extends over this chart exactly when its pullback to the double cover t²=s extends; the tame inertia of the double cover at t=0 is the subgroup of squares of the tame inertia at x (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.3a (tame inertia), EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.A1 (decomposition and inertia) and §F.3a (trait inertia)), so the pullback is unramified in codimension one exactly when the inertia image has order dividing two (Abhyankar's lemma, Stacks 0EYG).
A finite étale cover of the punctured regular chart that is unramified in codimension one extends uniquely to a finite étale cover of the chart (Stacks 0H2W); the extension is μ₂-equivariant by uniqueness and descends along the atlas (§7.4 (lisse descent and finite-cover monodromy)).
The stabilizer μ₂ at x is the image of the local inertia, so it acts on the stalk by χ|I_x̄. By Noohi Theorem 7.11 the quotient of π1(𝒳) by the closed normal subgroup generated by the stabilizers is π1(X), which gives the descent criterion.

R=∅: 𝒳=X and the statement is the ordinary dictionary between local systems on X and representations of π1(X). X=P¹, R={0,∞}: over k̄, 𝒳≅[P¹/μ₂] for the squaring map, and the admissible geometric characters are the trivial one and the quadratic Kummer character of t ramified at 0 and ∞. A character whose inertia at some x∈R has order four is excluded. With R=∅, X=ℙ¹ over 𝔽₅ and E=ℚ₃, the rank-two local system on which Frobenius acts by J=[[1,1],[0,1]] is in the domain of the statement and is not a sum of rank-one local systems; its restriction to every nonempty open subscheme keeps the two-dimensional endomorphism algebra of matrices [[a,b],[0,a]].

For d=2 and a two-dimensional degree-one space, signed invariants are spanned by e₁⊗e₂−e₂⊗e₁, dimension 1. Ordinary symmetric invariants have dimension 3. Over ℚ̄₂ the factor 2 is invertible; over 𝔽₂ the square tensor e₁⊗e₁ is signed-invariant and is not an exterior image.

## Layer 8: High-degree effective descent

### 8.0 The scheme projective-space input

Prove that for every algebraically closed field K and every r≥0, every connected finite étale cover of ℙ^r_K has degree one. For r=0 the only connected finite étale K-algebra is K; for r=1 Riemann–Hurwitz gives 2g(Y)−2=−2m, so g(Y)=1−m≥0 forces m=1. For r≥2 apply gap:normal-proper-hyperplane-covers to a hyperplane ℙ^(r−1)⊂ℙ^r. Every connected finite étale cover stays connected on that hyperplane, where induction forces degree one. This supplies the scheme input to the weighted quotient argument in §§8.7 and 8.9. (SGA1 line 8606, Exposé XI, Proposition 1.1, printed p.285, recomposed p.219; SGA1 line 8303, Exposé X, Lemme 2.10, printed p.274, recomposed p.210; SGA1 line 8308, Corollaire 2.11.)

- For ℙ⁰_K, a connected finite étale algebra has degree 1, whereas the degree-two algebra K×K is disconnected.
- For a cover of ℙ²_K, restriction to a line stays connected by Corollaire 2.11; on that ℙ¹ the equation g=1−m excludes m=2 by giving −1 and leaves m=1 with g=0.
- The image-dimension hypothesis in the general hyperplane contract is necessary: over ℂ, the map ℙ¹→ℙ¹, t↦t², pulls back the point 1 to {1,−1}, with two connected components. Its image has dimension 1, outside the contract.

For a C-torsor Q a B-torsor lift with a quotient identification exists exactly when δ_N¹[Q]=0 in H²(K). This class is independent of τ, and vanishes exactly when [L] is in the image of d_* on H¹(B).

### 10.30 The double projective line degree test

Let k be finite of odd characteristic and ν:ℙ¹_k→ℙ¹_k be t↦t², with σ(t)=−t and R={0,infinity}. The line O(1) upstairs is σ-invariant but is not pulled back from the base: pullback multiplies degree by 2. Hence q_*[O(1)] is nonzero although j_*q_*[O(1)]=0, and lies in image(δ_N⁰). The same holds for O(−1). Norm preserves degree and sends O(1) to O(1); these statements do not contradict the obstruction-sensitive torsor fibres.

Use the corrected invariance criterion to locate their nonzero K-torsor classes in image(δ_N⁰).
The ordinary finite-flat norm sends the degree-one point 0 upstairs to the degree-one point 0 downstairs. The line/divisor norm comparison gives Nm O(1)=O(1).

- For M=O(−1), the same parity obstruction gives −1∉2ℤ, excluding a hidden restriction to effective degrees.
- Nm O(1)=O(1) has degree 1. A norm that doubled degree would give degree 2 and fail this test.

### Examples

For t²=a, multiplication by c+dt has matrix ((c,ad),(d,c)), determinant c²−ad². At a=0 it is c². On the cover ℙ¹→ℙ¹, t↦t², the invariant upstairs line O(1) cannot descend because pullback degrees are even: 1≠2m for every integer m. At an inert unramified point the anti-invariant Frobenius scalar is −1, at a split point +1; on x−y the trace is their quotient.

## Downstream consumers

Root-stack specialization and section-conjecture applications, in the form of Bresciani's birational section conjecture arguments, consume the infinite DVR gerbe and its Kummer classification (§§3.190–3.191). The quadratic character sheaf on the root Picard stack and its Frobenius trace (§§10.20–10.24) are the geometric class field theory input of the ramified Taylor-expansion theory of Yun–Zhang. These applications supply no input to this build.

## Worked examples

For A=ℤ/4, n=2, a zero root section with power-identification coefficient 3 exists on the trivial line. The units 1 and 3 both have square 1, so neither normalizes that identification over A. Adjoining z with z²=3 gives the finite free fppf normalization cover. This distinguishes a stack quotient from an orbit set of A-valued chart points. A chart is a μ₂-torsor over the root stack; the chart's map to Spec A need not be a torsor when the section vanishes. (AGV08 line 2431, Appendix B.2, pp.53–54; FramedRoot-codex-rtOQ9t line 7989, Example 4.9.22.)

On X=𝔸¹_𝔽ₚ with divisor x=0 and exponent p, the smooth frame atlas has equation zᵖ=qx with q invertible. Eliminating x yields 𝔽ₚ[z,q,q⁻¹], a regular smooth atlas; the finite μ_p chart itself is not the smooth atlas. The stack is regular and tame, while its branch inertia is non-étale. For s=2 on Spec ℤ at exponent 3, every branch point lies in V(2), where 3 is invertible, so the stack is DM even though 3 is not globally invertible. On a stack base B𝔾_m with s=1, the relative root is the base itself and still has its base automorphisms. (AOV08 line 906, Definition 3.1, and line 910, Theorem 3.2; AGV08 line 2431, Appendix B.2.)

For factorial restriction, a root of order 6! = 720 induces a root of order 5 by the 144-th tensor power, since 5·144 = 720. Passing through order 5! = 120 gives exponent 6 followed by 24, whose product is again 144. The tensor-power comparison supplies the arrow between these section-bearing roots. Over a field k, on the zero-section chart, z_nʳ≠0 whenever 0≤r<n. Every element of the root-coordinate ideal is nilpotent because it comes from one finite stage, but the ideal has no uniform nilpotence exponent: for any r choose n>r. (TV17 line 650, Proposition 3.5 and Remark 3.6; line 702, §3.1.)

For a zero-section root y in a chosen frame, write φ(eⁿ)=aλ. A normalized coframe has coefficient b with bⁿ=a, while an arrow from the chosen trivial root to y has coefficient c with acⁿ=1. Its band-preserving Kummer class is therefore [a⁻¹]. At n=3, a=2 over ℚ this is [1/2], whereas the coframe class is [2]; their ratio 4 is not a rational cube. Replacing λ by 3λ gives [3/2]=[3][1/2]. Replacing a DVR uniformizer π by uπ rescales the normal-line frame by u⁻¹ and shifts by [ū⁻¹]. (STACKS-KUMMER line 1442, Lemma 59.28.3; B24, pp.135–136, cited by locator alone.)

Over ℝ, a compatible band point satisfies ζ_n=ζ_(2n)²=1, so the infinite trivial root has no nonidentity real automorphism. The finite even-degree components nevertheless have automorphisms ±1. The Kummer class system has two compatible possibilities, the trivial system and ([−1]_n)_n. Thus a neutralized infinite gerbe has two real isomorphism classes, each with trivial real automorphism group. The second is represented by the torsor tower z_nⁿ=−1, whose odd levels are trivial. (STACKS-KUMMER line 1442; TV17 line 733, Remark 3.9; B24, pp.135–136.)

For the root Picard section quotient over 𝔽₅, take γ=α=1 and change the root frame by u=2. The coordinates become (γ′,α′)=(4,2), and γ′⁻¹α′²=4·4=1, agreeing with the original squared evaluation. On ℙ¹ with one rational branch point and L=O(−1), a root line on R and a nonzero root section still exist, even though H⁰(ℙ¹,O(−1))=0. A section only on R is therefore distinct from an effective global divisor section. (YZ19 line 6968, Appendix A.1.2, p.515.)

Over 𝔽₃[ε]/ε² in the split high-degree chart, (u,α)=(0,ε) is a nonzero tuple whose section coordinate is (0,0), so it lies outside the effective open. The tuple (1,ε) is effective and keeps its nilpotent root coordinate, although its section coordinate is (1,0). Changing the evaluation splitting by t changes the kernel coordinate from u to u−t(α²), a quadratic coordinate transition that respects weights (2,1). (YZ19 line 7536, proof of Lemma A.9, p.521; StacksBaseChange line 2818, Lemma 30.22.1.)

For the cover ℙ¹_𝔽₅→ℙ¹_𝔽₅ given by t↦t² with R={0,∞}, global root units are (c,v₀,v∞) with c=v₀²=v∞². There are 2·2·2=8 such units. Norms of global upstairs units have form (w²,w,w), giving an image of size 4. The unit c=(1,1,−1) is outside that image, so its connecting K-torsor class is nonzero and has order two. If a norm trivialization changes by τ_new=c⁻¹τ, its based fibre class changes by this connecting class. The quotient obstruction in H²(A)/im(δ_q¹δ_N⁰) is independent of the choice, whereas the obstruction for a fixed norm trivialization remains in H²(A). The upstairs line O(1) is invariant but has degree 1, outside the pullback degrees 2ℤ. (YZ19 line 7850, Appendix A.3.3, pp.524–525; MILNE-LEC, §9 property (c), pp.64–66 and §11, pp.76–79.)
